title: Is Private Equity Cooked? | Andreessen Horowitz
gist: a16z's Jen Kha argues tech buyout is a late-cycle asset class now structurally impaired: 2021-22 vintages are levered, flat and PIK-ing, appraisals lag, exits take ~7 years, and top-5% venture beats top-5% buyout on DPI and TVPI. Advice: find exits from 2021-22 buyouts and, if allocating to venture, only be in top-tier managers.

insights.claim: Over the last 10 years US buyout returned 14.5% a year, underperforming the Russell 3000, while US venture pooled across all funds returned 17.6% a year, unlevered.
insights.speaker: Jen Kha
insights.so_what: Benchmark LP allocations: buyout has lagged public markets despite leverage.
insights.quote: In contrast, US venture as a whole returned 17.6% a year
insights.locator: What's left when you turn on the lights

insights.claim: A top-5% US venture fund (2007-16 vintages) delivered 5.3x DPI versus 3.5x for a top-5% buyout fund, and nearly 2.2x better TVPI.
insights.speaker: Jen Kha
insights.so_what: Manager selection in venture matters far more than asset-class median; compare best-to-best.
insights.locator: What's left when you turn on the lights

insights.claim: Venture track record stays a meaningful predictor of the next fund's performance, whereas since 2000 a top-quartile buyout fund has not reliably predicted the next one (Harris, Jenkinson, Kaplan & Stucke 2023).
insights.speaker: Jen Kha
insights.so_what: Persistence supports re-upping with proven VCs but not automatically with buyout managers.
insights.locator: What's left when you turn on the lights

insights.claim: Tech buyout is a late-cycle asset class that works once a technology wave has settled and cash flows are predictable enough to borrow against; when a new wave arrives venture outperforms, as in the dot-com bust vintages (~1998-2005) when venture trailed.
insights.speaker: Jen Kha
insights.so_what: Timing framework: venture leads at the start of a tech wave, buyout late; the author places us at the start of the AI wave.
insights.quote: Tech buyout is a late-cycle asset class.

insights.claim: In H1 2026 venture funds marked their tech companies up 16% while buyout funds marked their tech holdings down 4%.
insights.speaker: Jen Kha
insights.so_what: Marks show diverging stress between the two strategies.

insights.claim: PE-backed middle-market companies carry 4.7-6.0x adjusted EBITDA in net debt across 2019-25 vintages, roughly 2.5-3x the median S&P 500 company's ~2x (J.P. Morgan).
insights.speaker: Jen Kha
insights.so_what: Leverage amplifies sensitivity to growth and rates.
insights.locator: What's left when you turn on the lights

insights.claim: For stressed PE-backed borrowers that are adding interest to the loan (PIK), loan-to-value rose from 44% to 75% in a year.
insights.speaker: Jen Kha
insights.so_what: PIK accrual is the early indicator to ask managers about on 2021-22 vintages.

insights.claim: 70% of debt foreclosed in 2025-26 came from 2021 or 2022 deals, and private equity backed 54% of the largest US corporate bankruptcies (liabilities of $1B+) in 2025.
insights.speaker: Jen Kha
insights.so_what: Vintage year, not manager quality, explains much of the distress.

insights.claim: Thoma Bravo bought Medallia in 2021 for about $6.4 billion and this year handed it to lenders led by Blackstone, wiping out about $5.1 billion of equity, showing even top software operators could not make a 2021 deal work.
insights.speaker: Jen Kha
insights.so_what: Credit funds taking the keys and buyout funds losing equity can sit in the same LP portfolio, so risk just moves pockets.

insights.claim: About $140B of risky loans owed by PE-backed companies mature in 2028 and another $160B in 2029, versus an average ~$60B coming due two years out in 2023-25; about a third is software and a quarter is rated CCC+ or below.
insights.speaker: Jen Kha
insights.so_what: A refinancing wall in 2028-29 is the catalyst to watch for software LBO credit.

insights.claim: PE valuations are set by the owners themselves, so struggling companies can be held flat, whereas venture marks rise only when outside investors lead a higher-priced round.
insights.speaker: Jen Kha
insights.so_what: Treat PE NAVs with a discount; compare with public BDC and loan pricing.
insights.quote: more fiction has been written in Excel than in Word

insights.claim: Continuation vehicles made up 14% of PE exit value in H1 2026, up from 5% in 2020 (Jefferies), as sponsors sell to funds they also manage when no outside buyer shows up.
insights.speaker: Jen Kha
insights.so_what: Rising reliance on continuation funds signals weak third-party exit demand.

insights.claim: Some funds borrow against the whole portfolio (NAV loans) to return cash to LPs, flattering distributions without any company being sold while adding a second layer of debt.
insights.speaker: Jen Kha
insights.so_what: Check whether DPI is being funded by NAV facilities.

insights.claim: Software-heavy BDCs trade well below NAV and default rates range from 1-3% to ~15% depending on definition, while realized losses are still under 1%, meaning losses have not yet been taken.
insights.speaker: Jen Kha
insights.so_what: Public BDC discounts are a real-time read on private marks.

insights.claim: PE exits now average about 7 years versus 5-6 years in 2010-21, and PE-backed tech exit value is down 77% from a year earlier; about half of 2025 US PE exits by count were sales to another sponsor.
insights.speaker: Jen Kha
insights.so_what: Slower exits depress DPI and extend LP capital lock-up.

insights.claim: Buyout returns in the 2010s relied on falling rates and rising multiples (Bain: over 50% of returns); a typical 2015 deal needed ~5% annual EBITDA growth for 2.5x in five years, but today's deal needs 10-12% because debt costs more and entry prices are no longer falling.
insights.speaker: Jen Kha
insights.so_what: Underwriting math has worsened; '12 is the new 5'.

insights.claim: Golub Capital's software borrowers slowed from 9% revenue growth to under 3% in two years, so the growth underwritten in 2021 deals is not materializing and EBITDA support is margin-driven.
insights.speaker: Jen Kha
insights.so_what: Margin expansion helps pay interest but doesn't justify entry multiples.
insights.locator: Maybe it's cyclical, maybe it's structural

insights.claim: Would-be strategic buyers of application software have weakened share prices, while able buyers are acquiring new technology (Nvidia-Hugging Face at $13B, SpaceX-Cursor at $60B), leaving old software 'on the shelf'.
insights.speaker: Jen Kha
insights.so_what: Exit routes for legacy SaaS LBOs are narrow.
insights.locator: Maybe it's cyclical, maybe it's structural

insights.claim: Buyout fundraising fell 16% in 2025 to $395 billion and remained weak at midyear 2026; tech rose from 23% of buyout deal value in 2018 to about a third after ChatGPT, and PE has since begun retreating from tech.
insights.speaker: Jen Kha
insights.so_what: Capital formation in buyout is contracting.
insights.locator: Maybe it's cyclical, maybe it's structural

insights.claim: Many top buyout firms are public companies, and the scoreboard has quietly shifted from outperformance through returns to a business valued on AUM.
insights.speaker: Jen Kha
insights.so_what: Incentives favor fee-earning AUM over returns.
insights.locator: Maybe it's cyclical, maybe it's structural

insights.claim: Moving from buyout into private credit or secondaries does not escape the problem: private credit loans to SaaS grew from ~$8B in 2015 to over $500B by end-2025 (BIS) with capped upside, and secondaries mostly buy buyout stakes at a discount.
insights.speaker: Jen Kha
insights.so_what: Substitution into credit/secondaries keeps exposure to the same companies.

insights.claim: Anthropic raised $65 billion in a single round in May, more than the $56.6 billion Electronic Arts take-private, the largest buyout on record per Bain.
insights.speaker: Jen Kha
insights.so_what: Venture-scale rounds now rival the largest buyouts.

insights.claim: Venture is riskier at the median, so exposure only makes sense in the top 5% of managers; 'proximity to venture does not equal participation in its rewards'.
insights.speaker: Jen Kha
insights.so_what: Concentrate VC allocation in top-tier managers or skip.
